title: Student accommodation in Berlin
description: Dorms, shared flats and private rentals in Berlin: current rents, the best areas for each university, temporary options, address registration and how to avoid scams.
html:
Berlin has more students than any other German city and not nearly enough rooms for them. Finding a place is possible, but it takes a plan, an early start and a healthy suspicion of offers that look too good. Here is how the market works in 2026.

Types of accommodation

Rooms in the student services residences cost around €300 to €450 a month and are the cheapest option, with waiting lists of a semester or more. Private student residences charge €600 to €900 for a furnished studio and can usually be booked from abroad. Rooms in shared flats run from €450 to €700 depending on the area. A one-bedroom flat of your own starts around €900 and requires the full landlord document set.

Applying for a dorm

Apply through the student services organisation as soon as you have your admission letter, choose several residences to widen your chances, and respond to any offer within the stated deadline, which can be a few days. Applications from abroad are accepted; a German bank account is needed for the deposit later.

Areas by university

For the university in the south-west, look at Steglitz, Dahlem and Wilmersdorf. For the technical university and the university of the arts, Charlottenburg and Moabit are close. For the university in the centre and the big hospital campus, Mitte, Prenzlauer Berg and Wedding work. Neukölln, Friedrichshain and Lichtenberg are cheaper and well connected to everywhere. The public transport network makes a 30-minute commute from almost any district realistic.

Temporary options

Most students arrive without a permanent room. Hostels, short-term sublets and temporary student housing bridge the first weeks; some temporary providers allow address registration, which matters, so ask.

Registering your address

You must register (Anmeldung) within two weeks of moving into a permanent address. You need an appointment at a citizens' office, your passport and a confirmation from the landlord. Appointments in Berlin are scarce; book online early and check for cancellations. Registration produces the certificate that your bank, insurer and immigration office will ask for.

Staying safe

Never pay a deposit before viewing the room or before a platform has verified the landlord. Be wary of landlords who are "abroad" and want money by transfer to release keys. Use platforms with payment protection when booking from outside Germany. If a rent looks far below the figures above, assume a scam.
